name: Vision Cone Example
miniText: What information is available to an agent that can only perceive objects ahead? NetLogo Vision Cone Example uses the in-cone primitive to filter nearby turtles or patches according to distance, heading, and angular extent. Reynolds [1] develops autonomous-agent steering with local perception, Couzin and colleagues [2] study collective motion with directional interactions, and Couzin and colleagues [3] examine leadership under local information. These papers supply scientific settings in which the demonstrated geometric filter matters; the example itself does not implement their complete behavioral models. Changing heading rotates the eligible region, while radius and angle independently limit perception. Occlusion, sensory errors, and species-specific detection are additional assumptions absent from a simple cone query. The simulation illustrates a perception boundary that can be reused in models, rather than evidence that real agents perceive every object inside an ideal geometric sector.
